approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs using only the current task's accepted scores. It chooses parents from high-scoring population quantiles, builds a surplus pool through connected-fragment crossover or local atom/bond mutations, and keeps a bounded population of the best observed molecules. Ordinary single-parent proposals sample one, two or three successive mutation calls; prolonged unsuccessful pool filling can raise that floor. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen exchange is disabled. Stable canonical identities and duplicate rejection govern admission. A Gaussian posterior over integer-count Morgan fingerprints, using generalized Tanimoto similarity, learns from the full accepted archive. Correlated posterior score draws then select distinct pool members for each announced batch.
approach.novelty: This control removes optional ordinary mutation continuation: when the saturation floor is one, the first mutation-call result proceeds to the existing admission and selection path without a second or third call. The original length draw remains, and higher-floor recovery, internal mutation retries and crossover finishing mutation remain intact. Earlier siblings removed crossover, sampled residual influence, residual correlation or fingerprint multiplicity. This experiment instead isolates ordinary continuation on their shared exchange-free Parent. A historical continuation removal lost endpoint score on an exchange-enabled composition; the new test asks whether the retained route still contributes here. The predicted loss concerns endpoint search, even if first-product acceptance or local parent-beating yield improves.

observed_bottleneck: The Parent n-62daf219c70a devotes real proposal effort to optional successive mutations whose current-composition contribution remains unisolated. Its actual three summary.json/run.log pairs are complete, with macro mean 0.5956696497334577 and population SD 0.02659287062806747. A read-only audit of all fifteen Parent task logs, excluding emitted copies from generation counts, finds 75961 breeding attempts, including 41627 ordinary single-parent attempts. Of these, 7499 execute multiple calls: 6261 execute two and 1238 execute three. Their 7423 pooled paths yield 322 accepted descendants, 46 parent beats and 20 incumbent improvements; 135 of these accepted identities later breed. Maximum consecutive member attempts is five, so no higher-floor saturation opportunity occurs. These useful products support testing positive contribution, but their selected-cohort outcomes do not identify the value of omitted continuations. Historical n-29d770e728a6 correctly removed continuation and lost 0.019179888857869958 in paired mean against its exchange-enabled Parent, with seed deltas -0.024068018734495933, -0.039844558853128986 and +0.006372911014015048; its non-inferiority prediction failed and seed two improved every task. Different composition/profile prevents treating that result as the current contrast. Current sibling n-767d2ce08797 removed crossover, retained continuation and lost 0.054937284705486644; it cannot isolate continuation. The limitation addressed is this retained route's unresolved endpoint contribution, not a demonstrated absence of useful multi-call products.
hypothesis: Remove optional second and third successive GraphOperators.mutate calls from ordinary single-parent proposals when the inherited saturation floor is one, retaining the original sampled base-length draw and the full max(base length, saturation floor) schedule whenever that floor exceeds one.

finding_summary.headline: Ordinary continuation contributes to endpoint search: its removal lowers all three seed macros.
finding_summary.insights:
The removal exposed useful first products, yet useful local steps did not preserve final search quality. Across the whole Child, parent beats increased from 629 to 714 and incumbent improvements from 258 to 299 while endpoints fell. Those counts depend on changing ancestors and incumbents; they cannot tell us what the omitted continuations would have scored. This resolves the previously open current-composition contribution question, separately from the earlier exchange-enabled experiment. It does not make the separate crossover and posterior-component losses additive.

The molecular assessment helps narrow the next question to coverage of useful structural arrangements. The Child still finds varied aromatic, carbonyl and amine families, but its leading repeated aza-aryl family does not recover the Parent’s compact carbonyl-thione organization. Some other families improve, and reactive bonds, difficult ring geometries and unspecified stereochemistry persist on both sides. Fewer calls therefore do not establish chemically simpler or more feasible output. These associations do not identify which omitted product or molecular feature caused the score loss. Saturation recovery remains untested, and fewer calls did not yield an observed speedup: total wall time was about 1,778 seconds versus 579, alongside much greater oracle time on the changed molecules.
finding_summary.results:
Ordinary second and third mutation calls disappeared under real requests for longer walks. The Child made one call in all 41,665 ordinary attempts; 7,373 requests would have allowed continuation, suppressing 8,589 requested calls. The Parent actually executed 8,737 continuation calls. Of the affected first-call products, 6,980 entered the candidate pools and 518 reached accepted evaluation; 100 beat their generating parent and 35 improved the incumbent. Internal retries, crossover finishing mutations and correlated posterior selection remained active. Neither side exercised saturation recovery.

The complete matched three-seed panel fell from mean final Top-1 0.595670 to 0.568802, a paired change of -0.026868, exceeding the registered 0.002 loss scale. Seed changes were -0.047714, -0.009154 and -0.023735. Population dispersion decreased from 0.026593 to 0.012088, but every seed macro was lower. Ten task-seed endpoints declined and five improved: all three median_2 endpoints, zaleplon_mpo in seed zero, and sitagliptin_mpo in seed one. Three task means declined and two rose. Correct execution and the predicted endpoint loss support a positive contribution from retained ordinary continuation in this composition.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families persist, with enlarged repeats, unusual N-halogen bonds, strained rings and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: For n-dbee08307e86, all supplied Child and published Parent n-62daf219c70a trajectory paths were present and read. The brief independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, and no profile-mismatched seeds. No task is omitted and no comparison path is missing. Each task supplies 900 Child records, including 870 optimizer records; the Parent panel is also complete. The paired files share their fixed initial molecules and scores. The digest final_molecules are late seed-2 proposals, not the retained best molecule for every seed; the full trajectories determine the per-seed descriptions below. Output includes compact aromatic ketones and amides, very large repeated aza-aryl ethers, linked carbonyl-rich heterocycles, flexible and cyclic polyamines, fused or bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino heterocycles. Child ring-closure-string incidences are 0.9713, 0.9782, 0.9839, 0.9839 and 0.9644 in the fixed task order; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9701, 0.9782, 0.9828, 0.9782 and 0.908. These are incidences of SMILES text features, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0 throughout, although available aliphatic amines and potentially stereogenic saturated centres occur. Size and ring descriptions were checked with the locked RDKit environment directly on these trajectory graphs; this does not establish synthesis, conformation, stability or biological activity. Ring and aromatic content are rich. Structural diversity is moderate across tasks and seeds, but leaders within a seed commonly share a scaffold. Drug-likeness is weak overall because familiar medicinal functional groups coexist with N-halogen bonds, peroxides, repeated large assemblies and difficult small-ring or bridged geometries. The Parent already exhibited these general concerns: its full report and the original n-c55c3d520a2c molecular report were read through the evidence index. Their historical origin is retained in each transferable gap; older-profile evidence is not another current replica. The current Child changes the realized chemical families, including a much larger repeated aza-aromatic family and a fluorinated leader without the Parent leader's cyclic cumulene. It does not establish uniform chemical improvement or loss. All literal molecular citations below are Child molecules allowed by the digest or trusted citation_trajectory_paths; Parent-only structures are identified descriptively by task/seed/evaluation in the published trajectories. Chemistry associations here do not identify activation, attribute a liability to ordinary continuation, assign scores to omitted products, or isolate a mediator of the paired endpoint contrast. The audit is .slots/r0016-02-ablation-L01/molecular/trajectory_audit.json; inspected_records.json retains every read graph, score, source path and descriptive calculation.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-1 leader (evaluation 296) is a compact aza-indole-like fused aromatic system attached through an alpha-fluorinated ketone to pyridine; it carries vinyl, methyl and ethyl groups and fluorine on the fused-ring nitrogen. Seed 0 instead retains an indole/azaaryl amide with an additional fused saturated four-membered carbocycle, methoxy and fluoromethyl substituents, and an N-chloro or N-fluoro amide. Seed 2 reaches a benzene-fused unsaturated four-membered carbocycle bearing vinyl ether, methylamino and alpha-bromo ketone substituents. Thus most leading material is compact, aromatic and carbonyl-containing, not deficient in rings or heteroatoms. Mean Child SMILES length is 42.4 and halogen-string incidence is 0.8667. The Parent seed-0 leader (evaluation 289) instead contains an amino-substituted cumulene; its seed-1 leader (293) is an N-hydroxy pyridyl amide and its seed-2 leader (294) a vicinal diketone. The Child seed-0 endpoint is higher, while the other matched seeds are lower. Both panels retain questionable local chemistry on recognizable aromatic frameworks.
liabilities: N-F on the fused heterocycle and N-Cl/N-F on an amide are distinct from conventional aromatic C-F/C-Cl substitutions and raise environment-specific stability and synthesis concerns.

The alpha-halo ketones are potentially electrophilic, while the seed-2 unsaturated four-membered fused carbocycle raises a geometric concern. A saturated fused four-membered ring is a different case and is not rejected merely for its size.
Vinyl ether, N-N-containing nearby variants and unassigned saturated centres complicate the chemical interpretation of otherwise familiar aromatic molecules.
missing_features: High-scoring, conventional local substitutions preserving the favorable aromatic/carbonyl organization are not consistently demonstrated; ordinary N-H indole amide chemistry is present initially, so this is a reliability gap rather than an inability to produce an amide.
Explicit stereochemical identity is absent for the alpha-halo ketone centres, and the small unsaturated fused-ring arrangement lacks demonstrated accessible geometry.
The available gradient does not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore or support simply increasing rings, donors or halogens.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. The small difluoroacetanilide (seed 1, evaluation 22) scores 1.1981624660071522e-08, and the tiny FCl proposal scores 0.0. Useful reward therefore accompanies a combined fused aromatic/carbonyl/pendant aromatic arrangement in these examples, not carbonyl or fluorine presence alone. Within the seed-1 ketone family, adding alpha fluorine changes the observed score from 0.4425635194548914 to 0.46092619585962435. The seed-0 N-chloro and N-fluoro amides share exactly 0.44742068512417055; their tie does not establish that either N-halogen bond is required. The different seed-2 alpha-bromo ketone shows that the leading set is not exclusively an N-halogen series, although it has its own local reactivity and ring concerns. Matched retained best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.44742068512417055 / 0.39405142067435733; seed 1: 0.46092619585962435 / 0.47411701813450596; seed 2: 0.4254027310763201 / 0.438972502037081. These are supplied endpoint observations, not molecular mediation estimates.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (evaluation 283) is an oligomer-like chain of methylated pyridyl rings joined by aryl ethers and acyl-carbonate linkages, with a terminal chlorinated azaaryl region. It is a very large repeated assembly rather than a compact fused heterocycle. Seed 1 retains a fused nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl system attached to a small oxygen-containing fused ring and a long oxygen/acyl-rich substituent. Seed 2 retains a fused nitrogen dione attached to an aryl-pyridyl ketone and a sulfur-containing unsaturated cyclic imine, with a chlorinated alkyl substituent and either ethoxy or ethylperoxy termination. Mean Child SMILES length is 91.2, with a maximum of 219; the Parent report gives a mean of 59.1. Published Parent seed 0 (evaluation 281) instead has a much more compact linked aza-aromatic/fused carbonyl-thione structure with O-F and halomethyl-ether liabilities; Parent seeds 1 and 2 have other compact linked aromatic families. The Child misses that Parent seed-0 organization in its leaders and instead elaborates repeated azaaryl material. This is changed output coverage, not a demonstrated chemical explanation of the endpoint difference.
liabilities: Very large repeated azaaryl scaffolds and the duplicated late scaffold add substantial molecular bulk and connectivity without a corresponding clear local score gain; distinct repeat counts do not establish independent scaffold diversity.
Peroxide connections and acyl-carbonate/anhydride-like connections raise stability concerns. The recognizable diaryl ethers alone do not establish a feasible route for the whole assembly.

The smaller Child seed-1 family still contains a very small oxygen-containing fused ring and numerous acyl/ether bonds; compactness is not a sufficient synthesis criterion. The Parent compact leader also has reactive O-F chemistry, so it is not a validated chemical target.
missing_features: Reliable access to compact, distinct linked heterocyclic arrangements is not demonstrated across the Child leaders; the favorable compact Parent seed-0 family is absent from that leading set.

The repeated azaaryl and carbonyl-rich assemblies do not show controlled simplification while retaining useful chemical context. A smaller ethoxy example already provides a counterexample to the need for extensive repetition.
Stable alternatives to peroxide and densely connected acyl-oxygen environments are not consistently retained, although the ethoxy counterpart proves that an ordinary ether is already accessible.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl fused dione scores 0.548381482770623, a small aromatic acyl-carbonate proposal scores 0.5152505446623094, and methane scores 0.5. The large seed-0 azaaryl chain reaches 0.6069792671166827, but size alone is not a reliable reward direction. Seed 2's ethoxy example scores 0.6049255191910405 and its ethylperoxy counterpart 0.6057651321398124. The peroxide is therefore not necessary for a very similar observed score within that family. A late seed-2 structure that repeats much of the full linked heterocycle system scores 0.6049312519383852, offering no substantial visible advantage over the much smaller ethoxy example. The observed rise is associated with retaining combined aromatic/heterocyclic context; it does not justify maximizing ring multiplicity or rewarding reactive links. Matched retained best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.6069792671166827 / 0.8561477222467935; seed 1: 0.5861615748583445 / 0.6248206599713055; seed 2: 0.6057651321398124 / 0.6178024026512013. These are supplied endpoint observations, not molecular mediation estimates.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader (evaluation 298) is a relatively compact flexible tertiary amine linking chlorinated phenyl groups, one phenolic, with an additional terminal imine. Seed 0 instead produces an anisole/halobenzyl polyamine containing an aziridine, an N-CH2-N linkage and a piperazine ring. Seed 1 reaches compact fused small nitrogen rings linked to an aryl-substituted cyclobutene and a sulfur centre bearing both S=C and S=O bonds. Available basic amine centres, saturated rings and aromatic surfaces are already abundant; formal-charge-string incidence of 0.0 does not mean these molecules lack protonatable sites. Mean Child SMILES length is 64.2 and halogen-string incidence is 0.9885. Parent leaders are a flexible halogenated aryl tertiary amine (seed 0, evaluation 284), an aminoalkyl pyrrolidine/aryl ether (seed 1, 261), and a pyrrolidine/fused thioether/biaryl system (seed 2, 241). Both panels therefore reach aryl-amine chemistry, but the Child leaders include more small-ring polyamine or unusual sulfur arrangements. Its flexible leader is a counterexample to any claim that fused small rings are required.
liabilities: An aziridine can be a real synthetic target but its strained nitrogen ring and N-CH2-N linkage require environment-specific reactivity assessment; graph validity is not that assessment.
The seed-1 S=C/S=O centre, fused small rings and cyclobutene are an unusual combination with no demonstrated route or conformation.

The flexible leading tertiary amine avoids N-halogen and complex fused rings, but still carries an imine, chlorinated aryl surfaces and unspecified stereochemistry. High supplied scores do not establish stability, selectivity or exposure.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified forms of the aryl/amine arrangements and saturated small-ring centres are absent. Neutral SMILES also leave physiological protonation unspecified, which is separate from whether a basic centre exists.

Consistent conventional local chemistry around the useful aryl-amine arrangement is not established: the seed-0 leader has an aziridine/aminal-like connection, seed 1 unusual sulfur and small-ring geometry, and seed 2 an imine.
The output does not lack basic cyclic or acyclic amines; the evidence supports preserving their useful molecular context and testing plausible alternatives, not simply adding more nitrogen.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An acid/amide-containing N-sulfinyl pyrrolidine (seed 0, evaluation 30) scores 0.0006372822060865817, while the aziridine/piperazine polyamine reaches 0.9882868043166894. A smaller sulfur-bound N-O-ring example scores 0.0035245283879830683; the larger aryl-linked small-ring amine with the same unusual S=C/S=O motif reaches 0.9838336855175471. The flexible aryl tertiary amine reaches 0.9929316871171222. Taken together, the visible positive association is an available aliphatic amine presented with substantial aromatic context, rather than nitrogen, halogen or sulfur count alone. A late N-N-linked relative scores 0.2676905798258133, and chloroethane scores 0.004326296390568256, showing that neither general polyamine elaboration nor a halogen fragment preserves that reward. These nonmatched chemical comparisons do not identify affinity, a required charge state or a binding pose. Matched retained best scores, Child / Parent, are seed 0: 0.9882868043166894 / 0.9999989177995104; seed 1: 0.9838336855175471 / 0.9969753164881906; seed 2: 0.9929316871171222 / 0.9999934235240012. per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (evaluation 292) joins a propylphenyl region and an ethoxy-substituted dihydrobenzofuran region through a saturated fused nitrogen-ring/dicarbonyl system with N-methyl amides. A nearby family contains an additional imine/N-N segment. Seed 1 uses a biaryl substituent attached to partially unsaturated medium nitrogen rings bearing dicarbonyls; seed 2 retains a more densely bridged diaryl nitrogen/dicarbonyl system with an N-N bond. These are medium-sized, ring-rich molecules containing both aromatic and saturated regions. Mean Child SMILES length is 57.0 and halogen-string incidence is only 0.1322. The Parent also reaches bridged nitrogen-carbonyl systems, including a diaryl N-O-containing leader (seed 0, evaluation 293) and quinoline-linked dicarbonyl/amine families (seeds 1 and 2, evaluations 278 and 261). Each matched Child retained best is higher, even though difficult topology and unspecified stereochemistry remain. This counterexample prevents describing the chemical change as uniformly detrimental.
liabilities: Dense fused/bridged connectivity, medium rings and ring-bound unsaturation create geometry and route questions even when the amide and ether groups are conventional.
Several nearby leaders introduce N-N or N-O environments, while the highest seed-0 example does not; these bonds must be assessed locally rather than treated as synonymous with nitrogen enrichment.
The potentially stereogenic saturated centres remain unspecified. Their existence is distinct from a demonstrated stereochemical score penalty.
missing_features: The Child does not consistently demonstrate simpler, accessible connectivities that retain the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/dicarbonyl organization; related leading structures still depend on fused or medium-ring systems.
Defined stereochemistry and conformational identity of the saturated ring junctions and bridges are missing.

Plausible independent alternatives within a seed remain limited among the leaders, but the different seed families and the saturated leader without N-N chemistry rule out global scaffold collapse or a universal reactive-link requirement.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-2 leader (evaluation 267) is a compact fused nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl heterocycle attached to a substituted cyclopentadiene. It contains fluoromethyl groups, an exocyclic imine and an N-F bond. Its carbocyclic double bonds are not cumulated. Seed 0 instead produces a fluoromethyl amidine attached through a diene ring to a fused aza/carbonyl system with N-F substitution and a pyridyl region. Seed 1 reaches an aromatic-labelled large nitrogen ring bearing carbonyl groups and an imine-bearing carbocyclic fragment with an unusual small-ring closure; this leader has carbon-bound fluorine without N-F. Mean Child SMILES length is 50.1 and cumulated-double-bond-string incidence is 0.0184. The Parent seed-2 leader (evaluation 273) has a small cyclic cumulene attached to a large aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring, whereas its seed-0 leader (276) has an N-fluoro fused imino/carbonyl core and its seed-1 leader (290) a fluorinated fused dione. The Child seed-2 leader therefore avoids the Parent leader's cyclic cumulene, while remaining below its supplied score; the Child seed-1 endpoint instead improves. A less conspicuous graph liability is not a measured score benefit.
liabilities: N-F bonds occur on leading fused-ring nitrogens, and the imine/amidine-rich local environments require stability and tautomer assessment.

A very small unsaturated carbocyclic ring is embedded in the seed-1 aromatic-labelled fragment; aromatic notation does not establish an accessible geometry. Seed 0 also retains a small fused aza ring.

The improved representation of one local feature, such as removal of the Parent leader's cyclic cumulene from the seed-2 leader, coexists with other liabilities and does not certify the whole molecule.
missing_features: Conventional stable nitrogen substitution preserving the favorable compact imino/carbonyl/fluorinated organization is not reliably established among the best examples; one seed leader lacks N-F but still has unusual ring geometry.

The aromatic-labelled large nitrogen ring and small unsaturated ring closures lack demonstrated geometric and tautomeric identity. The noncumulated seed-2 leader proves that generation is not limited to cyclic cumulenes.
Potential stereogenic ring centres are unspecified, and the observed score ordering does not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore or justify importing a target-specific structure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed here in n-dbee08307e86 against that published Parent on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. Historical origin is not additional replication. Current leaders include N-F on aromatic or amide nitrogens, N-Cl amides, alpha-halo ketones, peroxides, an aziridine/aminal arrangement and unusual S=C/S=O substitution. Counterexamples matter: a conventional ethoxy analogue closely approaches its peroxide relative, a high-scoring flexible aryl tertiary amine avoids N-halogen bonds, and a leading fluorinated family in one seed uses only carbon-bound fluorine. These are selective bond-environment concerns, not absence of amines, heterocycles or ordinary halogen chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently retain conventional local bond environments while preserving useful aromatic, carbonyl and amine relationships.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide bond-environment-aware transformations and plausible local alternatives that preserve favorable relationships learned from the current task's feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens and ordinary amine centres from reactive heteroatom-halogen or highly strained arrangements. No blanket halogen, nitrogen, peroxide or small-ring ban, guaranteed score gain, or attribution to a particular retained or removed component follows from this association.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed here in n-dbee08307e86 against that published Parent on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. Historical origin is not additional replication. The current output includes benzene-fused unsaturated four-membered carbocycles, densely connected small nitrogen rings, bridged dicarbonyl systems, and an aromatic-labelled large nitrogen ring with a very small unsaturated carbocyclic partner. The current fluorinated leader lacks the Parent leader's cyclic cumulene, and a high-scoring flexible aryl amine avoids the dense small-ring systems, so difficult cyclic unsaturation is not universal. Recognizable saturated small rings also occur and are chemically distinct from problematic unsaturation patterns.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring construction does not consistently establish geometrically credible unsaturation and bridge connectivity alongside graph validity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring edits sensitive to ring size, bond geometry and bridge connectivity, with alternative connectivities that retain learned functional-group relationships. Aromatic labels and ring counts cannot supply the missing conformational evidence. This motivates evaluating feasibility, not prohibiting ring formation or treating lower apparent strain as an established endpoint benefit; the observed topology change does not isolate a molecular mediator.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed here in n-dbee08307e86 against that published Parent on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. Historical origin is not additional replication. Every current digest has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0. Alpha-halo ketones, substituted aryl amines, saturated aza rings, fluorinated carbocycles and bridged dicarbonyl frameworks nevertheless contain potentially stereogenic environments. Formal-charge-string incidence is also 0.0, but basic amine centres are visibly present; neutral notation is a separate issue and not evidence that basicity is missing.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator leaves stereochemical identity unspecified after creating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or explicitly resolve stereochemical identity when chemically appropriate, while distinguishing achiral or configurationally unstable environments. Treat protonation and tautomerism separately from stereochemistry. These records establish unspecified identity, not a measured penalty for unspecified stereochemistry or proof that enumeration improves the objective; any change would need its own task-agnostic evaluation.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed here in n-dbee08307e86 against that published Parent on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. Historical origin is not additional replication. Tiny methane, isolated halogens, methanol and chloroethane proposals remain low-scoring even late in the records. At the other extreme, leading output includes repeated methylpyridyl ethers with acyl-carbonate links and a late duplicated linked-heterocycle scaffold. The duplicated scaffold has nearly the same supplied score as a much smaller ethoxy member, and a compact flexible aryl amine is itself a leader. The Parent also contains floor fragments and oversized examples, so neither the existence of fragmentation nor all growth is newly attributable to this intervention.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful functional-group context while controlling fragmentation and repetitive molecular growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use task-local feedback to retain useful combinations of molecular regions while allowing simplification and replacement of dispensable repeats. The missing capability is consistent control of context loss and unnecessary elaboration, not a fixed molecular-size preference. Smaller molecules can retain reward and large linked molecules can be useful; neither a universal size cutoff nor a score benefit from simplification is established by this panel.

transferable_gaps.evidence: This concern originates in n-c55c3d520a2c and was carried by n-62daf219c70a. It is re-observed here in n-dbee08307e86 against that published Parent on the complete matched Search Seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per objective, batch size 10 and the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile with direct aromatic exchange disabled. Historical origin is not additional replication. Current leaders repeatedly vary alpha-carbonyl substitution, N-halogen identity, short side chains, repeat counts or nitrogen-ring closures on retained scaffold families. The Child leading set does not recover the Parent's compact linked carbonyl-thione organization in the corresponding repeated-azaaryl stream. Other seeds genuinely reach different frameworks, saturated and unsaturated relatives can both be useful, and all current matched dicarbonyl-family endpoints improve. The finding is uneven leading-family coverage, not universal collapse, inability to create rings or evidence that the Child chemistry is uniformly worse.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently provide chemically independent plausible alternatives to the leading scaffold family within a seed.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support scaffold transformations that reorganize learned favorable functional relationships into feasible alternative connectivities and evaluate them through the current task's feedback. Distinct canonical strings and different repeat lengths should not be treated as sufficient evidence of useful scaffold coverage. This conditional coverage gap does not establish that any specific search component caused convergence, that a missing Parent molecule was a suppressed product, or that more diversity necessarily improves the objective.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
